title: Wiley and Wiley, and seeing him in the Chicago Defender
summary: He recalls Wiley's wife, who danced and sang, and the Wiley and Wiley billing. Years later he saw Wiley's picture in the Chicago Defender, from Detroit.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: See, they tried with shows. You can't remember the wife's name? I can't remember her name. Yes, she's on the... I can't remember her name. Her name ain't on there? No. There's a record credited to Wiley and Wiley. Wiley and Wiley.
Wiley and Wiley. That's him and his wife. And you remember...
But I forget her name.

Wiley and Wiley. That's what they went in. They played together. She sang and played. But I can't remember... A brother might remember her name. Oh, yeah. He might, yeah. Yeah. He used to play an ass. He didn't play. That's a bad song. What's the bad song?
I mean, he could play.
Oh, yeah. Not just lose anything. And could play sound like two pianos.
Yeah.

I ain't no joke. I give a man credit with it, you know. Yeah. See. I happen to plug them records. We go around. I went around with it. And I happen to sell them from door to door. We go in. In them days, Chicago, they didn't have no joints. It was dry. They had bootlegs. Moonshine. Yeah. And we go in them places and he played and sell the records. Sell his records. That's the way he sold his records. That's...
Very interesting. Yeah. In Chicago.
Finally, 15 years later, I was reading the paper, the Chicago Defender, the color paper. And I saw his picture. I thought the man was there.
Why did they print his picture?
Give him a ride up in Detroit, you know.
Oh, yeah.
And I thought he was dead. Oh, this had been 20-something years ago. He could be dead. He could be dead. I never hear that. Yeah. I don't know where he went. I never... I often wonder where he went.
But they gave his life story in this newspaper. Defender.
Yeah.
His life story when he was born and so on and so on and everything.
Oh, I must find it. He's from Helden, Arkansas. Yeah.
Your brother told me so too. He's from Helden.
I helped him to sell that record. He made it here. I'm proud of him.
